title: My Daily Routine
grammarNote: This lesson covers reflexive verbs (levantarse, bañarse, vestirse, acostarse), telling clock time (son las…, es la una, a las… de la mañana, y media, cuarto para las…), frequency adverbs (siempre, casi nunca, todos los días), the present continuous (estar + -ando/-iendo), and ir a + infinitivo for near-future plans. It's built around describing a typical weekday and agreeing on a time to meet.

phrases.target: Me levanto a las seis de la mañana
phrases.native: I get up at six in the morning
phrases.phonetic: meh leh-VAN-toh ah las SEH-ees deh lah mah-NYAH-nah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Levantarse' is a reflexive verb meaning 'to get (oneself) up'; the pronoun 'me' shows the action happens to the speaker, and 'a las + [hour]' states clock time.

exampleSentence.target: Me levanto a las seis de la mañana todos los días.
exampleSentence.native: I get up at six in the morning every day.

phrases.grammarNote: Reflexive verbs like levantarse pair a reflexive pronoun (me, te, se...) with the conjugated verb: me levanto, te levantas, se levanta.
phrases.memoryHook: Me levanto sounds like 'lever' — pull the lever on yourself to get UP.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I get up at six in the morning
practiceItems.answer: Me levanto a las seis de la mañana

practiceItems.prompt: ___ levanto a las seis de la mañana.

practiceItems.answer: Me levanto a las seis de la mañana

phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Bañarse' is a reflexive verb meaning 'to bathe/shower oneself'; 'todos los días' is a frequency phrase meaning 'every day'.

exampleSentence.target: Me baño todos los días antes de ir a la chamba.
exampleSentence.native: I shower every day before going to work.

phrases.grammarNote: Frequency expressions like 'todos los días' usually go at the end (or beginning) of the sentence and don't change the verb conjugation.
phrases.memoryHook: Baño sounds like 'bath-no' — no skipping the bath, every single day.

phrases.native: I am working on a project
phrases.vocabularyIntro: The present continuous (estar + gerund) describes an action happening right now; -ar verbs like trabajar form the gerund with -ando: trabajando.

exampleSentence.target: Ahora mismo estoy trabajando en un proyecto importante.
exampleSentence.native: Right now I am working on an important project.

phrases.grammarNote: Present continuous = estar (conjugated) + gerund; -ar verbs take -ando, -er/-ir verbs take -iendo.
phrases.memoryHook: Trabajando ends in -ando, like 'and-on-going' — the action is ON right now.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I am working on a project
Tu compañero te pregunta qué estás haciendo en este momento en la oficina. ¿Qué le dices?

phrases.target: Voy a salir a las cinco y media
phrases.native: I'm going to leave at five thirty
phrases.phonetic: voy ah sah-LEER ah las SEEN-koh ee MEH-dee-ah
phrases.vocabularyIntro: 'Ir a' + infinitive expresses near-future plans ('I'm going to...'); 'y media' means 'half past' when telling time.

exampleSentence.target: Voy a salir a las cinco y media de la chamba.
exampleSentence.native: I'm going to leave work at five thirty.

phrases.grammarNote: 'Ir a + infinitivo' uses the conjugated form of ir (voy, vas, va...) followed directly by the infinitive verb, with no preposition change.
phrases.memoryHook: Voy a = 'I'm going to' — VOY sounds like 'voyage', you're heading toward that plan.

practiceItems.prompt: Translate: I'm going to leave at five thirty
practiceItems.answer: Voy a salir a las cinco y media

practiceItems.prompt: Voy a salir a las cinco y ___.
¿A qué hora piensas salir de la oficina hoy?
practiceItems.answer: Voy a salir a las cinco y media
